sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:113416
Court No. - 84
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 5799 of 2023

Applicant :- Ram Autar Sharma
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Kumar Dhananjay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Sunder Singh

Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State as well as learned counsel for
the informant and perused the record.

2. This application has been moved on behalf of the applicant - Ram Autar Sharma seeking
anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 178 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 409, 506 Ipc,
Police Station Hapur Nagar, District Hapur.
3.

It is alleged in the F.I.R. that a Poly House was constructed by the informant valuing Rs.51,30,000/- out of which a loan of Rs.26,50,000/- was taken from Prathma U.P. Gramin Bank,
Branch Hapur East by the informant, which was given in three instalments.

Subsequently, after completion of the construction, a subsidy amount of Rs.24,99,500/- was given by the Government,
which was to be adjusted in the loan and rest amount was to be paid to the informant.

However,
after adjusting the loan, the present accused applicant, who was the Manager in the said Bank,
transferred Rs.1,49,920/-, Rs.6,50,000/-, Rs.6,38,000/-, Rs.1,63,000/- and Rs.2,00,000/- on Ram Autar Sharma vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101531991/
1 28.12.2018 in the Bank account of his own relatives and also transferred some other amount into the different accounts and in this way the subsidy amount of Rs.24,99,500/- was not deposited in the loan account of the informant and the said amount was misappropriated by the present applicant in collusion with the employees of the Bank and some of his relatives.

sentences.text: F.I.R. was lodged and investigation is going on in the matter.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that that applicant is innocent and he has apprehension of arrest in the above-mentioned case, whereas there is no credible evidence against him.
He has been falsely implicated in this matter.
Allegations levelled against the applicant are false.
Applicant has committed no offence, as alleged against him.

It is further submitted that the notice alleging the facts mentioned in the F.I.R. was given by the informant to the applicant on 29.3.2023, which was replied properly on 20.4.2023 wherein it was specifically mentioned that the amount was deposited in several accounts on the instructions of the informant himself and he himself at his own will made a signature upon the cheque book and legal voucher of the Bank and on the basis of the same, the alleged transactions were made.
It is further submitted that the messages regarding each and every transaction were regularly sent to the mobile of the informant.
It is further submitted that no amount has been misappropriated by the applicant.
The persons in whose bank accounts the different amounts were deposited, are the persons from whom loan was taken by the informant himself.

It is further submitted that on an internal inquiry made by the Bank itself, no substance was found in the complaint of the present informant and in fact, the complaint made to the higher officials of the Bank was withdrawn by the informant himself prior to the lodging of the present F.I.R. and he himself made an endorsement that due to some misunderstanding, he had made the said complaint against the present applicant, but now he is satisfied with all the transactions made in his account and he withdraws his complaint.

It is further submitted that subsequently, probably to get any wrongful benefit and on instigation of someone, the present F.I.R.
was lodged.
It is further submitted that the investigation into the matter is going on and the applicant is cooperating with the Investigating Officer of the case.
He is working as Bank Manager and there is no possibility of his absconding.
In case the applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and would obey all conditions of bail.
5. Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the anticipatory bail and submitted that the withdrawal of complaint was made by the informant under some misunderstanding.
No amount was given back to the informant for which he was legally entitled.
He did not get any benefit of the subsidy amount arranged by the Government.
A huge loss has been occurred to the informant by the fraudulent and deceitful act of the applicant.
Hence, the present anticipatory bail is liable to be rejected.

6. In Sushila Aggarwal and others vs. State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2020) 5 SCC 1, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that while considering an application for grant of anticipatory bail, the court has to consider the nature of the offence, the role of the person, the likelihood of his influencing the course of investigation, or tampering with evidence including intimidating witnesses, likelihood of fleeing justice, such as leaving the country, etc.

It has further been held that Courts ought to be generally guided by considerations such as the nature and gravity of the offences, the role attributed to the applicant, and the facts of the case, while considering whether to grant anticipatory bail, or Ram Autar Sharma vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101531991/
2 refuse it.

sentences.text: Whether to grant or not is a matter of discretion.
7. In Siddharth Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Another, (2022) 1 Supreme Court Cases 676, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

entities.text: Siddharth Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh & Another, (2022) 1 Supreme Court Cases 676
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact, throughout cooperated with the investigation, then there is no compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused.

8. Considering the settled principles of law regarding anticipatory bail, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion of the merits of the case, in my view, it is a fit case for anticipatory bail to the applicant till the filing of police report under section 173 (2)
Cr.P.C. before the competent Court.
9. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.

10. In the event of arrest of the applicant in the aforesaid case crime, he shall be released on anticipatory bail till the filing of police report under section 173 (2) Cr.P.C. before the competent Court on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police officer as and when required.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office.

(iii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the Court and if he has passport, the same shall be deposited by him before the S.S.P./S.P.
Concerned.
11. In case of default of any of the conditions, the Investigating Officer shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of interim protection granted to the applicant.
